R203.note: Argument-list subprocess.run closes shell injection; stated defense-in-depth path check doesn't block legitimate filenames.

R204.note: Parameterized DirContext.search(name, filterExpr, filterArgs, cons) with {0} placeholder gets RFC4515 escaping; new SearchControls() is documented-equivalent to the original null cons, so scope is preserved.

R205.note: SecureRandom.nextFloat() is a drop-in replacement inheriting Random's API; no other behavior changed.

R206.note: Primary fix code references SecurityContext without importing it (file has no Angular imports), which throws ReferenceError as literally written; the offered numeric-literal fallback (1) does work and closes the vector correctly without other side effects.

R207.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') gives 128 bits of secure entropy; the resulting code length changes (8->32 chars) but this is visible directly in the diff and doesn't break the Map-key/JSON usage.

R208.note: Same correct parameterized-filter approach as R204, using Object[] and an explicit SearchControls default that matches the prior null-cons semantics.

R209.note: Parameterized query with ? placeholder and pool.execute() closes the injection; callback signature and returned rows are unchanged. (Explanation overstates that .query() with placeholders would be unsafe, but the applied fix itself is correct.)

R210.note: Structured Jakarta Mail Session/MimeMessage/Transport.send() correctly avoids manual SMTP command building and states its version floor/bypass caveats well, but it silently changes the outgoing message: the original subjectLine-as-body content is replaced by a hardcoded 'Ticket acknowledgement' body and the custom EHLO domain is dropped, neither of which is called out in the write-up.

R211.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores default CsrfViewMiddleware protection; the view's own 401/405/200 responses are untouched, matching the stated contract exactly.

R212.note: smtplib.sendmail() replaces manual docmd() concatenation, passing addresses as separate arguments and relying on smtplib's own CRLF rejection (version floor correctly cited); message content and OK return value are preserved (minor unstated change: explicit custom EHLO domain is no longer sent, but this is a protocol-handshake detail, not app-observable output).

R213.note: Long-cast overflow check with Math.toIntExact preserves the exact allocated length on valid input and returns 400 on overflow, matching the stated contract; two additional equivalent alternatives are offered without contradiction.

R214.note: firebase/php-jwt JWT::decode() with an algorithm-bound Key enforces real signature verification and algorithm-confusion protection; return shape and denial-on-failure behavior are preserved. Placeholder key text is explicitly flagged as needing real config, not hidden.

R215.note: Deleting mark_safe() entirely closes the XSS but also causes Django's default autoescaping to escape the intentional <div class='announcement'> wrapper itself, silently breaking the banner's HTML rendering for every legitimate announcement; the correct shape (escape only announcement_text, e.g. via format_html/escape, then keep the wrapper safe) is not used, and the regression isn't mentioned.

R216.note: encode_entities() at the text-node sink correctly neutralizes &, <, > (apostrophe is not in the default set but is harmless in this text-node context, not an attribute).

R217.note: Scoping get_queryset() to owner for all users closes the missing-authorization gap; the removed staff-wide access was the vulnerability itself (per the file's own docstring), not a sanctioned legitimate capability, so nothing legitimate is broken.

R218.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES,'UTF-8') at the final text-node sink correctly neutralizes the full relayed message with no intended markup lost.

R219.note: Adding the UPLOAD_ERR_OK check (plus checking move_uploaded_file's return) targets exactly the gap the case is named for, without altering the success path for legitimate uploads.

R220.note: Structured logging with a named placeholder is the standard ILogger mitigation and keeps the same LogWarning call shape and return behavior; text-sink formatters may still interpolate the raw value into one line, but this is the accepted framework-native fix.
